segments.text: Another cron job copies a password into temp, but this time the file name is computed at runtime, so I cannot just read it from the script.
I log in as bandit22 with ssh bandit22@bandit.labs.overthewire.org -p 2220.
It takes whoami, which is bandit twenty-three when cron runs it, builds the string I am user bandit twenty-three, hashes it with MD five, and uses the first field as the file name.
The note spells out the target: temp slash, the MD five of I am user bandit twenty-three.
The hash is deterministic, so I reproduce the exact pipeline myself: echo I am user bandit twenty-three, piped to md5sum.
I cat that file in temp.
It holds the password for bandit twenty-three, and the level is solved.
